name: Svc_IpcCmd200040
signature: unsigned int Svc_IpcCmd200040(unsigned int* session, unsigned char value)
summary: IPC request stub: writes header 0x00200040 (command 0x20, one normal parameter) and the byte value into the thread-local request block, issues svc 0x32 on *session and returns the reply word. Used by the two DSP service flush routines.
evidence: The names Svc_IpcCmd20040 (0x0011EB14), Svc_IpcCmd1100C2Read (0x0011EAB4) and Svc_IpcCmdD0082 (0x0011EB58), all confirmed in R_057, establish that this family is named Svc_IpcCmd<header hex>; this body carries the literal header 0x00200040, so the old Snd_IpcCmd20 wording both misspelled the header (0x00200040 vs 0x00020040 of its neighbour) and over-claimed the sound subsystem. Both callers are the DSP service flush pair passing the handle at g_dspServiceState+8.

name: Snd_SetupChannelBuffers
summary: One-time layout of the DSP stream buffers: optionally uploads the 0x1080-byte wave buffer, asks the driver for the channel count and the channel-id list, then splits the region into 24 blocks of 0xC0/0xC/0x20 bytes and stores the resulting pointer table plus the active double-buffer index at +0x1322.
evidence: Its sole caller is now named Snd_InitStreamContext (0x00112E38) and the +0x1322 selector it latches is read back by the named Snd_SetChannel* setters (Snd_SetChannelGain / Volume / Rate) to pick the channel block, so both the subsystem and the 'buffer setup' role are supported by named neighbours.

name: maybe_Svc_IpcStubFragment
summary: Not a function start: this is the tail of the preceding thumb IPC stub (store the word at (b>>1)+0x10, byte-swap the session handle, svc 0x32, read the reply at (b>>1)+4). No branch reaches 0x001149AA; it only appears as the body of the enclosing routine 0x001148F0.
evidence: Nothing changed: 0x001148F0 is still only maybe_Snd_CommandRing_Reserve, no direct branch targets 0x001149AA, and the body still starts mid-idiom, so the fragment reading cannot be upgraded to a real function name.

name: maybe_Os_HandleSyncResult
signature: void maybe_Os_HandleSyncResult(u32 result, u32 arg2, OsSyncObject* syncObject, char* pendingFlag)
summary: Result handler for a synchronisation wait: extracts the result class from the top bits and, on the normal path (object +0x14 bit 0 clear and the caller pending flag clear), maps class -1 to the assert helper and then runs the completion helper 0x0011C814; on the other path it asserts for every class except -7 and 1.
evidence: Renamed away from the predicate-sounding CheckSemaphoreResult: the function returns nothing, it either asserts or calls the completion helper 0x0011C814. It is still unreachable dead code (no caller, no branch target), so the semaphore attribution cannot be confirmed and the maybe_ prefix stays.

name: Svc_IpcCmd150082
signature: unsigned int Svc_IpcCmd150082(unsigned int* session, unsigned int unitFlag, unsigned int unitIndex, unsigned int extraWord)
summary: IPC request stub: header 0x00150082 (command 0x15, one normal plus two translated parameters), three payload words in the thread-local request block, svc 0x32, reply word returned. It is the write half of the read-modify-write done by the unit-flag setter.
evidence: Same family naming as Svc_IpcCmd20040 / Svc_IpcCmdD0082 / Svc_IpcCmd1100C2Read (confirmed R_057): the body carries the literal header 0x00150082, which is what the new name states; the old name wrote the command id but dropped the parameter descriptor. Sole caller 0x001123B0 passes enable and unitIndex as the two translated words.

name: Snd_SetChannelField1A
summary: Writes the 16-bit field at +0x1a of the channel block selected by the context's +0x1322 index and ORs 0x10000000 into its state word to mark it dirty; returns 1 when the driver session is open, 0 otherwise.
evidence: The sole caller is the named Snd_SetOutputMode (0x00112D98) and the block selection (ctx+0x1322 into the 24-entry pointer table at ctx+0x10a4, dirty bit 0x10000000) is identical to the named Snd_SetChannelGain / Volume / Rate setters, so the Snd_SetChannel* family placement is now proven; only the logical meaning of +0x1a stays unknown, which the name does not claim.

name: Svc_IpcCmd190000
summary: Parameterless IPC request: header 0x190000 (command 0x19, no parameters), svc 0x32, returns the reply word. Its only caller is the signal-and-close path, so it is the final notification before the session is closed.
evidence: The body states the whole fact the name claims (header literal 0x190000 and svc 0x32) and the family now has confirmed members named Svc_IpcCmd20040 / Svc_IpcCmdD0082 / Svc_IpcCmd1100C2Read, so the header-based naming is consistent instead of the previous 'IpcCmd19' which dropped the descriptor half of the header.

name: Svc_IpcCmd80082
signature: uint32_t Svc_IpcCmd80082(uint32_t* session, uint32_t word1, uint32_t word2, uint32_t word3)
summary: IPC request stub: header 0x00080082 (command 0x08, one normal plus two translated parameters), three payload words in the thread-local request block, svc 0x32, returns the reply word. The parameter meanings are not visible from the code.
evidence: Same family as the confirmed Svc_IpcCmd* stubs: the literal header 0x00080082 is in the body, which is exactly what the new name says, while the old Os_IpcCmd08 named the command without the descriptor and guessed the Os prefix.

name: maybe_std_ScalbnRoundTail
signature: double maybe_std_ScalbnRoundTail(u32 sign, u32 mantissaHigh, u32 mantissaLow, int exponent)
summary: Rounding/overflow tail of the double scalbn helper: conditionally increments the mantissa, propagates the carry into the exponent and saturates to infinity. The decompilation is damaged (unaff_r11 / in_CY) and no caller reaches it.
evidence: Unchanged: still no caller, and the body still reads the round bit from a lost carry flag (in_CY) and an unaff register, so the scalbn attribution remains an inference from the bit layout only.

name: Video_ConvertBlocks32_SamePlane
summary: In-place 32-bit-lane colour/format conversion: reads the four lanes 0x100 bytes apart at -0x200/-0x100/0/+0x100, blends them with 1:2:1 averages and saturating differences and writes the result back into the same plane.
evidence: The dispatcher that selects it is now named Video_ConvertSelectB_A (0x0012A84C, confirmed 0.55) and takes this branch exactly when the context's two pointers are equal, which is what 'SamePlane' describes; the _B/_C twins of the same body are already confirmed under the same scheme.

name: Video_ConvertBlocks16_A
summary: In-place 16-byte-block conversion for the first decoder instance: averages six neighbouring lanes 0x400 bytes apart and saturates the differences, writing back into the source plane.
evidence: Its dispatcher Video_ConvertSelect_A (0x0012A81C, confirmed 0.55) selects it when the context's two pointers are equal, and the byte-identical variants at the B and C decoder instances are already confirmed as Video_ConvertBlocks16_B / _C, which fixes this one as the _A member.

name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes4_A
summary: Plane-strided copy kernel of the first decoder instance: descriptor fields are {src, dst, rowLength, planeCount}; four rows of 8 words are copied per plane with a 0x400-byte plane pitch and a 0x3e0 row remainder. The '4 planes' in the name is not proven - only a 4-iteration row loop is visible.
evidence: The dispatcher Video_ConvertSelect_A (0x0012A81C) still only proves membership of the conversion family, not the plane count; the body is a pure u32 copy loop with no colour arithmetic, so 'Planes4' stays a description of the loop nesting, not a verified count.

name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes3_A
summary: Second plane-strided copy kernel of the first decoder instance: identical to 0x001290A0 except that the unrolled body covers two stride groups, giving the shorter 0x2344-byte form. Same 0x400/0x3e0 pitch constants.
evidence: No new caller or constant: the dispatcher Video_ConvertSelectB_A only proves the family, and the 3-vs-4 distinction is still a size/nesting observation, so the name is kept as a maybe.

name: maybe_Video_ConvertBlocks8_B
summary: Smallest member of the conversion family: 8-byte-block conversion reading four lanes 0x100 bytes apart (source at +0x800) with saturating 1:2:1 arithmetic. No branch target reaches it, so its dispatcher entry is not visible.
evidence: Still unreferenced by any named dispatcher or caller; only the lane offsets and the 0x20202020/0x01010101 constants tie it to the same family as the confirmed ConvertBlocks* kernels, which is not enough to drop the maybe.

name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes4_B
summary: Plane-strided copy kernel of the second decoder instance: same four-field descriptor and 4x-unrolled u32 copy loop as 0x001290A0 but with a 0x100-byte plane pitch and 0xe0 row remainder.
evidence: Only pitch constants differ from its twin, and the twin itself is still a maybe_, so confirming this one would just spread an unverified 'Planes4' reading; no caller or dispatcher reference exists for it.

name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes3_B
summary: Second plane-strided copy kernel of the second decoder instance: byte-identical to 0x00129EF4 apart from the 0x100/0xe0 pitch constants.
evidence: No new evidence: the body is a pure u32 copy loop, no caller or data reference exists, and the base copy at 0x00129EF4 is also still a maybe_.

name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes4_C
summary: Plane-strided copy kernel of the third decoder instance: same body as 0x0012CE18 with a 0x200-byte plane pitch and 0x1e0 row remainder.
evidence: No caller, dispatcher or constant reference resolves this address; it is one of the three byte-identical pitch variants, and the other two remain maybes.

name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes3_C
summary: Second plane-strided copy kernel of the third decoder instance: same body as 0x0012DC6C with the 0x200/0x1e0 pitch constants.
evidence: Still unreferenced and identical to its siblings apart from pitch; nothing in the named code selects this address.

name: maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupEven
signature: void maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupEven(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, int bitCount, u32 bitReservoir)
summary: Case body of the MPEG-style block decoder: consumes a 3-bit prefix from the bit reservoir, remaps the escape code and dispatches up to four sub-block decodes through the 16-entry table at 0x00135418, using the 0x0F3F1F00 sub-block presence mask. Reached only through a computed jump and damaged in the decompilation.
evidence: The neighbourhood is now readable (Video_DecodeSubblockMask, Video_IdctBlock4x4, Video_VlcDispatchEntry), which confirms the codec family, but this body still has no direct branch target and still relies on unaff_r6, so the even/odd grouping cannot be verified.

name: maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupOdd
signature: void maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupOdd(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, int bitCount, u32 bitReservoir)
summary: Other case body of the same block decoder: reads a 4-bit prefix, clamps it against the sub-block counts at f_51/f_58, rewrites the four current-code bytes and jumps through the shared 0x00135418 table. Heavily damaged decompilation (17 removed unreachable blocks).
evidence: The family is confirmed by the now-named Video_DecodeSubblockMask / VideoIdct neighbours, but the body still cannot be entered from any branch target and depends on unaff_r6, so the even/odd split is unproven.

name: maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4
signature: void maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4(const u32* src, u32* dst, int count)
summary: Packed-byte horizontal filter: computes 1:2:1 averages over four 32-bit words at a time with the 0x7F7F7F7F mask, adds the two scanline halves and advances in 0x400-byte steps, count/2 times. Internal kernel with no caller.
evidence: No caller, no named callee and no string reference exists for this address; the mask arithmetic is verified but the consumer of the filtered rows is unknown, so the name stays a maybe.

name: maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4b
signature: void maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4b(const u32* src, u32* dst, int count)
summary: Variant of the packed-byte filter that takes its samples from unaligned byte offsets (src-1, +3, +7, +0xB) before the masked 1:2:1 averaging, i.e. the shifted-phase companion of 0x00138324.
evidence: Still an internal, uncalled kernel: the only new context is the confirmed sibling names, which do not say which output phase each variant produces.

name: maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4c
signature: void maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4c(const u32* src, u32* dst, int count)
summary: Third variant of the packed-byte filter: same unaligned sample offsets as 0x0013849C but with 0x1010000 multipliers and 0x10/8 shifts, producing the half-sample phase row.
evidence: No caller or data reference; the phase it emits is still inferred from the multiplier constants only.

name: maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4d
signature: void maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4d(const u32* src, u32* dst, int count)
summary: Fourth variant of the packed-byte filter: 1:2:1 averaging with 0x10000 multipliers over halfword-aligned sources, i.e. the 16-bit-per-pixel counterpart of the other three kernels.
evidence: Still uncalled and unreferenced; the 16-bit reading comes from the 0x10000 multiplier and halfword loads, which is suggestive but not proof.

name: maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock
signature: void maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock(const u32* src, u32* dst, int count)
summary: Block-level packed-byte filter: the same masked 1:2:1 averaging as the word kernels but with two extra live accumulators, so one pass produces two output rows 0x100 words apart.
evidence: No caller or reference exists; the earlier alternative name Video_FilterRgbaBlock was dropped because the mask arithmetic works on any 8-bit channel layout, and nothing here shows RGBA specifically.

name: maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock2
signature: void maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock2(const u32* src, u32* dst, int count)
summary: Byte-granular variant of the block filter: same 1:2:1 arithmetic but samples are taken with byte shifts (>>0x18, *0x100), so it filters one 8-bit channel plane instead of packed words.
evidence: Uncalled and unreferenced; the byte-plane reading follows only from the shift amounts.

name: maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesFrame
signature: void maybe_Video_FilterPackedBytesFrame(const u32* src, u32* dst, int count)
summary: Frame-level pass of the packed-byte filter family: filters whole scanline groups and calls the block decoder 0x0013B4E4 (Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock_B) for the sub-block work, i.e. a post-filter that also drives the second decoder instance.
evidence: It now has one named callee (Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock_B) which puts it in the codec pipeline, but there is still no caller and the fact that it drives the _B instance from the _A address block means the instance mapping is not understood.

name: maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupOdd_B
signature: void maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupOdd_B(u32 block, u32 subblock, int bitCount, u32 bitReservoir)
summary: Second copy of the coefficient-decoder odd-case body, in the second decoder instance: clamps a 4-bit prefix against the sub-block counts at f_51/f_58 and jumps through the shared table. The decompilation is damaged (unaff_r6 plus 17 unreachable-block warnings).
evidence: Its base copy 0x001351C8 is still a maybe_ and this one is equally damaged, so naming it confidently would only duplicate an unproven label.

name: maybe_std_VprintfFloatHelper
summary: Helper reached only from the printf core: it forwards straight into 0x00100F04, which in turn wraps the CRT routine 0x003007B8 with a leading argument 0xC, i.e. the float/number formatting path of vprintf. The 212-byte extent is Ghidra padding, the body itself is a one-call thunk.
evidence: The only new context is that the caller is now named std_vprintf_core and the transitively reached routine is std_strtod, which makes a printf conversion helper likely, but the intermediate 0x003007B8 still has no readable body, so the exact conversion (float vs integer) is unproven.

name: maybe_Os_InitStringRecord
summary: Allocates/looks up record 0x04000027 (helper 0x00300308) and stores the two built-in string pointers at +4 and +0xC of it; the getters are the paired 0x00105238 and 0x00105280.
evidence: The record id 0x04000027 and the two pointer stores are verified, but both getters are still maybes (locale/region is their guess, not an established fact), so 'InitStringRecord' is as far as the evidence goes.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetFramePeriod
summary: Stores the same value into two fields of a context (+8 and +0x14) and then resets two unreadable counters through 0x00107894 / 0x00107880; no caller and no constant ties it to a frame period specifically.
evidence: Unchanged: the two callees still have no readable body, so neither the 'frame period' reading nor the Gfx subsystem can be confirmed.

name: maybe_Os_GetDefaultLocaleString
summary: Returns a pointer into the built-in string area (base at 0x00694910 plus a fixed offset), unless the caller supplies a non-empty override name that resolves through 0x0010540C, in which case it returns 0. Paired with 0x00105280 by 0x00102828.
evidence: The override-name logic is readable, but 0x0010540C is still unnamed and the string contents were never checked, so 'locale' remains the earlier guess.

name: maybe_Os_GetRegionString
summary: Structurally identical to 0x00105238 but pointing at the second built-in string (base 0x006949D8): returns the built-in pointer unless a non-empty override name resolves through 0x0010540C, then returns 0. It fills the second field of the record built at 0x00102828.
evidence: Same limitation as its twin: the string identity is not checked anywhere in the named code, only the pair-store in 0x00102828 connects the two.

name: maybe_Os_GetInitPhase
summary: Maps the global stage byte read by 0x001146F0 to 1 when it is zero and 2 otherwise. With 35 named callers spread over boot (Engine_Initialize), save (SaveWork_Container_BaseCtor), UI and field code it behaves like a global stage/phase query, not a subsystem flag.
evidence: The 35 named callers show it is a shared global query, which rules out any single subsystem name, but the byte at 0x007AE939 is only written by 0x00114700 (no readable body), so 'init phase' stays an inference from the 1/2 mapping.

name: maybe_Gfx_InitChannelQueue
summary: Initialises a ~0xA8-byte record: stores the handle, runs the two sub-object initialisers on +8 and +0x2C, writes -1 into the slots at +0x50, +0xA0 and +0xA4, links the object obtained from 0x001125BC and sets the byte at +0x98 to 1.
evidence: The recorded callee cluster is now input/HID (Input_SetPadMode, Hid_DispatchPadReport) rather than graphics, and the disassembly branches to 0x0010C4B8/0x001125BC/0x0010C660, none of which are the functions the dossier lists, so both the Gfx prefix and the 'channel queue' reading are doubtful.

name: Gfx_DispatchVramRegionRequest
summary: Routes a VRAM address to the allocator that owns it: tests the address against the 0x20000 and 0x30000 bank ranges using the bank base/end getters and forwards it either to the display-state child's vtable slot +4 or to the fallback helper 0x0010E66C.
evidence: Both bounds helpers it calls are now named (0x001109A0 Gfx_GetVramRegionEnd, 0x001109DC Gfx_GetVramRegionBase) and one caller is the named Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks, which fixes the function as a per-frame VRAM-address dispatch.

name: Gfx_GetVramRegionSize
summary: Returns the size of a 3DS VRAM bank: 0x180000 for bank 0x20000 and 0x280000 for bank 0x30000 when the extended-memory query succeeds, 0x300000 otherwise, and 0 for any other bank id.
evidence: The returned literals are exactly the three 3DS VRAM bank sizes and match the base/end getters (0x1F000000+0x180000, 0x1F300000+0x280000, 0x1F000000+0x300000); the bank id arrives in the condition flags because the seeded entry is not the real function start, which does not affect the name.

name: maybe_Snd_WriteChannelEntry
signature: void maybe_Snd_WriteChannelEntry(char* obj, unsigned int value, unsigned int extra)
summary: Damaged thumb stub: writes a halfword at +2 and, when the object's first byte is non-zero, mirrors a word into the CSND hardware state block and calls the channel-gain setter 0x00118D00. The decompilation uses unaff_r6/in_s0 and no branch reaches the seeded address.
evidence: Unchanged: the body is still damaged and unreachable, and its recorded callers (Input_Initialize, 0x001072C4) contradict the sound reading, so no confident name can be given.

name: Gfx_InvokeCallbacks
summary: Invokes the two registered callback slots (+0x40 with context +0x80, +0x44 with context +0x84) of the shared 0x007AE954 block, after optionally running 0x001139A0 when the incoming condition flag is clear.
evidence: Its sole caller is now named Mem_MapSharedBlock, and the counterpart 0x0010CB74 (Gfx_ResetStateBlock) clears the same block, so 'run the block's registered callbacks' is supported by named neighbours; only the Gfx attribution rests on those neighbours.

name: Gfx_ResetStateBlock
summary: Resets the shared 0x007AE954 state block: calls the GPU command helper 0x00114398 (Gfx_IpcCmd50100 family) and then clears the 28 state/counter words at +0xC..+0x3C and +0x4C..+0x7C plus +0x48 and +0x88, leaving the callback slots alone.
evidence: Nine callers, among them the named Gfx_UpdateDisplayState and Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks, and the cleared block is the same one whose callbacks Gfx_InvokeCallbacks (0x0010CB30) runs; the FS callers only show the block is also used by the shared GPU job path.

name: maybe_Container_ResetObject
summary: Resets a record in place: clears the 16 state words at +0x38..+0x74, calls 0x00116AE0(self, 0x84) twice, then sets +0x84/+0x85 to zero and the sentinel -1 at +0x88. No Ghidra body and no caller list exist for this entry, only this recovered reconstruction.
evidence: Nothing new can be checked: the address has no readable Ghidra body, no caller and no callee names, so 'Container_ResetObject' remains a description of a generic clear-and-sentinel reset rather than a proven role.

name: Gfx_GetVramRegionEnd
summary: Returns the inclusive end address of a 3DS VRAM bank: 0x1F2FFFFF for bank 0x20000 and 0x1F5FFFFF for bank 0x30000, 0 for other ids. The symbol starts 4 bytes into the real function (0x0011099C), which is why the bank id arrives in the condition flags here.
evidence: Disassembly, not just pseudocode, shows the whole fact: cmp r0,#0x30000 at 0x001109A8 with movne r0,#0, bl 0x0011981C and the literal-pool words 0x1F5FFFFF at 0x001109D0 and 0x1F2FFFFF at 0x001109D4. It is a plain getter; the in_ZR argument is only an artefact of the seed starting 4 bytes into the real function at 0x0011099C and there is no damaged code. Seven graphics-memory callers (InitHeaps, Mem_FreeGraphicsBlock, Gfx_Bch_LoadMeshData, Gfx_ModelResource_Parse) agree.

name: Gfx_GetVramRegionBase
summary: Returns the base address of a 3DS VRAM bank: 0x1F000000/0x1F180000 for bank 0x20000 and 0x1F300000/0x1F380000 for bank 0x30000 depending on the extended-memory query, 0 for other ids. The real entry is 0x001109D8, four bytes earlier.
evidence: Disassembly confirms it: cmp r0,#0x20000 and cmp r0,#0x30000, bl 0x0011981C, then ldrne/ldreq from the literal pool whose words 0x1F380000, 0x1F300000 and 0x1F180000 sit at 0x00110A1C..0x00110A24, plus moveq r0,#0x1F000000 at 0x00110A14. This is a plain getter with no damaged code; the flag-register argument only comes from the seed starting at 0x001109DC instead of the real entry 0x001109D8.

name: maybe_Snd_SetUnitFlagBit
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetUnitFlagBit(unsigned int handle, unsigned int enable, unsigned int unitIndex)
summary: Read-modify-write of one bit of the service bitmask cached at g_dspServiceState+0xC: builds 1<<(enable+unitIndex), rejects the request with 0xC8A0A7F8 when the bit is already in the wanted state, otherwise pushes the change through Svc_IpcCmd150082 and updates the cache.
evidence: The service-block and bitmask mechanics are now readable and Svc_IpcCmd150082 states the exact IPC call, but the six callers are a mix of pad readers (Input_UpdatePadState, Hid_ReadPadState), buffer code and DSP stream setup, so neither the Snd prefix nor the per-unit reading can be confirmed.

name: maybe_Gfx_CommandListWorker_Interior
signature: void maybe_Gfx_CommandListWorker_Interior(u32 ptr, u32 b, u32 value, u32 value2)
summary: Not a function start: interior code of 0x00114AB4 that byte-swaps a pointer and stores values relative to it (word at +0, then the same value four times at +0x1C..+0x28). No caller and no data reference points at 0x00114B12.
evidence: Unchanged: the only 'caller' is the enclosing routine 0x00114AB4, which is itself still a maybe_, so this can only be described as an interior fragment.

name: maybe_Snd_ReleaseBufferPairs
summary: Releases the three (pointer,size) buffer pairs of a sound object (+0x58/+0x34, +0x60/+0x3C, +0x100/+0x40) through 0x00116DA4, but only when bit 0 of the owns-buffers byte at +4 is set, so a caller-supplied buffer is never freed.
evidence: Both callers are now named sound functions (Snd_StreamVoice_Update, Snd_SetBgmVolume), which contradicts the previous Gfx prefix and places this in the sound/stream buffer path; the three (address,size) argument pairs are explicit, but the object type is still unknown, so the maybe_ prefix stays.

name: Svc_IpcCmd863Request
summary: Convenience wrapper for fixed IPC command 0x0863: fetches the current session handle with 0x0011709C (Os_AssertAndGetSessionHandle) and calls Svc_IpcCmd8630000, which writes the reply word to *out.
evidence: The callee used to be an unknown 0x00117098; the disassembly at 0x00117078 shows it is the assert-and-get getter that returns the session word, which is then dereferenced by Svc_IpcCmd8630000 (header 0x08630000, svc 0x32). That makes the wrapper's role explicit and drops the guessed 'Os_' prefix.

name: Os_AssertAndGetSessionHandle
summary: Asserts that the global object at 0x007AEA3C is non-zero (otherwise 0x0011ED40 with 0xE0A046DB) and returns its second word, which callers use as the IPC session handle.
evidence: 0x00117078 uses exactly this result as the session pointer for Svc_IpcCmd8630000, which dereferences it and issues svc 0x32 - so the returned word is a session handle, not a generic 'state'. 0x00117098 is the same getter entered four bytes early.

name: maybe_Os_WorkQueue_ProcessPending
summary: Scans the occupancy bitmap of the global work table (live count f_88, bitmap f_80, 0x14-byte records at f_7c) and re-submits every live record whose +0x11 flags clear 0x18 and whose first word is non-zero by calling 0x0011B530; with a non-zero argument it first runs the submit helper once.
evidence: The bitmap walk is fully readable, but the table base comes from a lost register (unaff_r4) in the decompilation and the two callers (Input_ReadPadState, Save_AsyncReadWorker) are only users, so 'work queue' is a reading of the data structure, not a proven subsystem.

name: Snd_QueryChannelInfo
signature: unsigned int Snd_QueryChannelInfo(unsigned int command, unsigned int in, unsigned int size, unsigned short* outCount)
summary: Forwards a channel query to the DSP driver when the session is open and returns its status; when no session exists it writes 0 to the output count and returns 0xC8A0A7F8.
evidence: Its only caller is now the named Snd_SetupChannelBuffers (0x0011302C), which calls it twice to obtain the driver buffer count and the channel-id list, and the request goes out through Snd_SendIpcBuffer with command 0x10 - three independent confirmations of the sound/driver role.

name: Snd_FlushChannels
summary: Per-frame DSP service flush: if the service is active, submits the final unit configuration through the 0x1100C2 command, runs the eight registered flush callbacks at 0x007E7998, clears the pending byte and sends the closing command 0x20.
evidence: The body operates on g_dspServiceState, calls Svc_IpcCmd1100C2Read through the locked wrapper and closes with Svc_IpcCmd200040 - all now named sound-service pieces; the caller 0x00113A50 is a per-frame update. That pins the Snd prefix and the flush role.

name: Gfx_GetQueueStatus
summary: Returns the pending byte at +1 of the queue object selected by index from the TLS array at +0x5C (the buffer the GSP command queue keeps per slot).
evidence: Its only caller is now the named Gfx_SwapFrameBuffers (0x00109E28), which reads this byte to decide whether a frame buffer switch may proceed, fixing both the Gfx prefix and the queue-status role.

name: maybe_MisSeededThumbStub
summary: Mis-seeded entry: the decoded body is a single 'return 0x4C' although 0x13E thumb bytes are claimed, and the recorded callers are list destructors and sound code, so the address does not describe a real function of its own. Treat the address, not the name, as unreliable.
evidence: The 12 callers (Snd_ReleaseAllChannels, Container_IntrusiveList_Clear, Ui_Widget_DestroyChildren, Container_Tree_Destroy, ...) are a destructor cluster, not HID readers, and the body is a constant return; the previous 'Hid_ThumbReader' label cannot be right, but no correct role can be derived either.

name: maybe_Hid_NormalizeCirclePad
signature: int maybe_Hid_NormalizeCirclePad(int axisX, int max, int axisY, int value)
summary: Normalises a circle-pad vector: subtracts the deadzone from both axes, compares the squared magnitude with the scaled limit, takes an integer square root by Newton iteration and scales both axes to 0x80, returning the radius.
evidence: The deadzone/sqrt/scale-0x80 arithmetic is readable, but the second axis and both outputs travel through unaff registers and there is no caller, so neither the parameter order nor the HID attribution can be confirmed.

name: maybe_Hid_SetVibration
summary: Stores a vibration request: keeps the larger of the two float amplitudes at +0xB8, copies it to +0xBC, stores the pattern word at +0xC0 and zeroes the phase counter at +0xC4 after notifying 0x0011CBD4.
evidence: The float arguments arrive in s0/s1 (silently dropped by Ghidra) and the recorded callee is a generic helper, so only the +0xB8..+0xC4 layout supports the vibration reading; kept as a maybe.

name: maybe_Os_EnsureInitialized
summary: Only a Ghidra index entry exists for this address (no readable C, no body, no callers or callees recorded), so nothing about its behaviour can be verified and the earlier 'ensure initialized' guess is unbacked.
evidence: No readable file and no call/callee information at all; the entry is kept only so the address is covered.

name: maybe_Mem_FreeThroughCallback
summary: Releases a heap block through the registered deallocator slot at 0x007AE9FC (clearing the slot first), then issues svc 0x3C. The real entry is 0x0011C814, four bytes before the seeded address.
evidence: The body is readable enough to show the callback-slot free, and the sole caller is now named Mem_CommitAllocation, but the deallocator itself has no readable body, so the exact allocator contract is unproven.

name: maybe_Gfx_CallNoOpStub
summary: Thunk that calls 0x00115E68 with argument 0; that target disassembles to 'mov r0,r0; bx lr', i.e. the default empty implementation of an interface, so this invokes the no-op default. The 802 recorded callers are an xref artefact of the overlapping branch range.
evidence: The empty target is verified by disassembly, but the interface it stands in for is unknown and the real call sites cannot be separated from the xref noise, so no better name is available.

name: Svc_IpcCmd8630000
summary: Fixed IPC request: header 0x08630000 (command 0x0863, no parameters) on *sessionHandle, svc 0x32; on success copies the reply word at TLS+0x88 to *out and returns the status word at TLS+0x84.
evidence: The literal header and the reply copy are both in the body, and the family convention Svc_IpcCmd<header hex> is established by the confirmed stubs Svc_IpcCmd20040 / Svc_IpcCmdD0082 / Svc_IpcCmd1100C2Read; the only caller is now named Svc_IpcCmd863Request.

name: Os_WaitSemaphore
summary: Counted semaphore wait with owner hand-off: a negative count means waiters, so the waiter decrements under ldrex/strex, arbitrates through 0x0011CC10 and flips the sign back when the count turns positive; on the fast path it simply negates the count.
evidence: The negative-count convention plus the exclusive-monitor loops and the arbitration call are the classic CTR semaphore shape, and the matching release/try-lock functions (Os_LockSemaphore, Os_TryLockSemaphore, Os_SignalSemaphore) are already named in this block.

name: Snd_SendIpcBuffer
signature: int Snd_SendIpcBuffer(unsigned int* session, unsigned int value, unsigned int zero, unsigned int address, unsigned short size, unsigned short* outSize)
summary: Submits a buffer descriptor to the sound driver: header 0x001000C0 (command 0x10 with one normal and one translated parameter), temporarily overwrites the thread's translated-descriptor words at +0x180 with size<<14|2 and the buffer address, sends svc 0x32, restores both words and copies the reported size to *outSize.
evidence: Its only caller is now the named Snd_QueryChannelInfo (0x001185E8), which uses it to fetch the driver's buffer count and channel-id list, and the header literal 0x001000C0 is exactly 'command 0x10 with a buffer parameter' - both the sound prefix and the buffer-send description are supported.

name: maybe_Snd_FlushChannelsOnStop
summary: Stop-time variant of the DSP flush: clears g_dspServiceState first, then - if the service had been active - submits the final unit configuration, runs the eight registered flush callbacks, clears the pending byte and sends the closing command 0x20.
evidence: The sequence matches the now-named Snd_FlushChannels (0x00118788) except for the upfront global clear, but the 41 callers are generic OS/FS/Gfx teardown paths, so whether this is really the sound-service stop or a shared 'abandon session' step cannot be decided.

name: Svc_IpcCmd130042
signature: int Svc_IpcCmd130042(unsigned int* session, unsigned int handle, unsigned int flags, unsigned int* out0, unsigned int* out1)
summary: IPC request with header 0x00130042 (command 0x13, one normal and one translated parameter): issues svc 0x32 and, on success, writes TLS+0x88 to *out1 and TLS+0x90 to *out0.
evidence: The header literal 0x00130042 is in the body, matching the established Svc_IpcCmd<header hex> family (Svc_IpcCmd20040, Svc_IpcCmdD0082, Svc_IpcCmd1100C2Read), and the caller list is a Gfx command cluster rather than the guessed 'Os' status query.

name: maybe_SlotTable_ReleaseSlot
summary: Releases one slot of a shared slot table: takes the table lock (0x0012032C), resolves the slot pointer for the index (0x00120368), takes the lock again and stores -1 into the header word 0x98 bytes before the resolved pointer to mark the slot free.
evidence: The body is clear, but the 16 callers span containers, UI, effects, FS and event handles, which contradicts the previous Gfx_CmdList label and instead points at a generic slot/pool table; the table owner is still unknown, so the name stays generic and uncertain.

name: maybe_Os_TranslateMainRamAddressInterior
summary: Not a function start: interior code of 0x00123E18 (Os_TranslateMainRamAddress) repeating its bounds comparison of addr and addr+base against the lower/upper main-RAM limits, returning the translated address or 0.
evidence: The enclosing routine is now named Os_TranslateMainRamAddress (0x00123E18, confirmed in R_039), which fixes what this fragment belongs to; the fragment itself still depends on unaff_r5 and the incoming carry, so it is not independently callable.

name: std_UnwindPersonalityRoutine
signature: u32 std_UnwindPersonalityRoutine(void* state, void* ucb, void* context)
summary: ARM EHABI personality routine: calls the unwind bytecode interpreter 0x001250BC with the inline personality opcode words that follow the call, and returns the unwind reason code (continue / handler found). It is referenced from .ARM.exidx tables rather than called, which is why the recorded caller count is an artefact.
evidence: The shape is decisive: push {r4,lr}, bl to the unwind interpreter, then .word 0x80xxxxxx personality opcodes inline - that is exactly the compact-model personality routine layout, and it explains the 80 'callers' as exidx pseudo-references instead of real calls.

name: maybe_std_CopyPointerListAndSync
summary: Copies a count-driven list of double-dereferenced pointers (descriptor[1] array, descriptor[2] count) into the caller's buffer in two unrolled passes, then either waits on the single handle (svc 0x24) when count == 1 or forwards to 0x001169DC with the descriptor's remaining fields.
evidence: The copy and the special count==1 path are readable, but 0x001169DC has no readable body and there is no caller, so what the descriptor's other fields mean stays unknown.

name: Video_McPredict1ApplyMv2
signature: void* Video_McPredict1ApplyMv2(McCtx* ctx, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Sub-block 2 of prediction variant 1: copies the stored motion vector (ctx+0x3bc/0x3c0) to the output pair and emits one luma and one chroma block through the filter-bank tables, using (mvX + 2*x) & 7 and mvY & 1 as the fractional filter index. It is an internal entry of the variant-1 ApplyMv routine, not an independent API.
evidence: Its caller is now the confirmed Video_McPredict1ApplyMv (0.52), and the three already-merged C-instance twins (0x00140E10/0x00140F34/0x00141058 etc.) are confirmed as Video_McPredict1ApplyMv2_C, so this entry gets the same scheme in the A instance.

name: maybe_Video_VlcDispatchEntry
summary: VLC coefficient-switch entry: loads the decoder context, reads the sub-block presence mask 0x02000F00, runs the bit-reservoir advance helper 0x001354DC and then branches through the unrecovered jump table at 0x00135418 to the per-sub-block decoders.
evidence: Its neighbour set is now named (Video_DecodeSubblockMask, Video_IdctBlock4x4, Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock), which confirms the codec, but the jump table itself is unrecovered and the body uses in_r12, so 'VlcDispatchEntry' stays a description of the dispatch, not a proven symbol.

name: maybe_Video_CoefficientSwitchTail1
summary: 36-byte shared tail of the coefficient-decode switch: an indirect jump through the relative table at 0x00135418 using the code index in r12. Not independently callable (incoming r12).
evidence: No new evidence: the body is a single table jump with in_r12 and no arguments, so it can only be described as a switch tail.

name: maybe_Video_CoefficientSwitchTail2
summary: 24-byte second shared tail of the coefficient-decode switch: relative jump through the 0x00135418 table using the code index in r12; reached from two dispatch entries.
evidence: Still only an indirect jump with in_r12; the named callers are itself a maybe_ dispatch entry.

name: maybe_Video_VlcDispatchEntry2
summary: Second VLC switch entry: uses the table index r12+10, loads the decoder context, tests the sub-block presence mask and branches through the 0x00135418 table. Damaged decompilation with unaff_r6.
evidence: Unchanged: the table is still unrecovered and the function is only reached from another switch tail, so the exact case it represents is unknown.

name: maybe_Video_InterpolateBlock4x4
summary: Unrolled sub-pixel interpolation kernel for a 4x4 block: builds per-column 6-bit fixed-point accumulators, advances a vertical phase DDA over the 16 samples and rounds with +0x10 before packing four output bytes per store.
evidence: The fixed-point DDA arithmetic is readable and belongs to the same decoder as the now-named Video_IdctBlock4x4, but the entry depends on lost registers (unaff_r11) and no caller or table reference selects this address.

name: maybe_Video_InterpolateBlock2x2
summary: Half-tap sibling of the 4x4 sub-pixel interpolator: same 6-bit fixed-point DDA scheme but with a 4-bit phase step and an 8-row loop over a narrower block, packing one output row per iteration.
evidence: Its only caller Video_DecodeSubblockMask (0x001352A0) is now named, which confirms the codec placement, but the block geometry in the name is inferred from the phase shift (4 vs 6 bits) while the loop still runs 8 rows, so the 2x2 wording is unproven.

name: maybe_Video_BlendPlanesDiag
summary: Intra-prediction blend kernel for the diagonal case: averages boundary samples at -1/+0x3FF/+0x7FF/+0xBFF with 1:2:1 weights and writes four packed bytes per scanline store into the 0x400-strided block.
evidence: The arithmetic is fully readable but the entry depends on unaff_r11 and there is neither a caller nor a table reference, so the 'diag' reading is a description of the averaging pattern only.

name: maybe_Video_BlendPlanesRow
summary: Row reconstruction kernel: blends the row above (at -0x400/-0x3FC), the top-left sample (-0x401) and the left sample (-1) into 1:2:1 averages and stores packed words for the current row.
evidence: Same situation as its siblings: readable 1:2:1 arithmetic, unaff_r11 base and no caller, so the row reading is inferred from the -0x400 access pattern.

name: maybe_Video_BlendPlanesRow2
summary: Second row-wide blend kernel: computes the plain horizontal averages of the row above first, then the diagonal 1:2:1 blends that use the left sample, covering two 0x100-word groups per pass.
evidence: Uncalled and unreferenced; the difference from 0x00136410 is visible in the arithmetic order but does not identify which prediction mode it implements.

name: maybe_Video_BlendPlanesRow3
summary: Third row-wide blend kernel: same 1:2:1 blend of the above row and the left sample, but with the intermediate averages kept in registers and stored in a different order across the 0x100-word scanlines.
evidence: Uncalled and unreferenced; only the register schedule differs from the sibling kernels.

name: maybe_Video_BlendPlanesBlock
summary: Block-wide blend kernel: expands the 1:2:1 averaging over a whole 4x4 block with all intermediates live in registers and writes each output row as one packed word.
evidence: Uncalled and unreferenced; the block-wide unrolling is visible, but nothing identifies the prediction mode.

name: maybe_Video_BlendPlanesFromStream
summary: Stream-driven blend kernel: advances the decoder bit reservoir (0x0013587C), then runs a 4-iteration loop that filters four scanline lanes with 4-bit phase accumulators and rounds with +0x10 before packing.
evidence: The callee set now includes the named Video_IdctBlock4x4, which places it in the decoder, but the entry still depends on unaff_r11/unaff_r6 and has no caller.

name: maybe_Video_BlendPlanesCorner1
summary: Top-left corner reconstruction: averages the upper-left sample (-0x401), the left sample (-1) and the row above to produce the corner word, then propagates the blended values down the first two columns of the 0x400-strided block.
evidence: Readable arithmetic with the -0x401/-1/-0x100 accesses, but no caller and a lost base register, so the corner reading is inferred from the offsets.

name: maybe_Video_BlendPlanesCorner2
summary: Byte-wise corner/edge blend kernel: first writes the horizontal 2-tap averages of the row above, then the 4-tap corner blends that add the left and upper-left samples, for four scanlines.
evidence: Uncalled, no named callee and a lost base register (unaff_r11); the arithmetic is identical to the sibling kernels, so the specific corner role cannot be separated from the other variants.

name: maybe_Video_BlendPlanesCorner3
summary: Simpler corner blend: writes only 4-tap (a+2b+c+2)>>2 results for the first word of each scanline, using the left, upper-left and above samples in a fixed rotation.
evidence: Uncalled and unreferenced, with the same lost base register as 0x001373C4; only the tap pattern distinguishes it, which is not enough for a role name.

name: Video_FilterPackedBytesRow
summary: Row-level intra-prediction filter: builds the horizontal 1:2:1 averages of the row above, then the 4-tap (a+2b+c+2)>>2 blends that also use the left sample, and stores four rows of packed bytes at 0x100-word spacing.
evidence: Both callers are now named decoder functions (Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock and Video_IdctBlock4x4), which fixes it as the row predictor of the video decoder; the name describes exactly the verified operation (packed-byte per-row filtering).
